newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MATCH ANALYSIS OF ATLETICO V REAL MADRID.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MATCH ANALYSIS OF ATLETICO V REAL MADRID.

text.p: Following is an analysis of the strengths and weaknesses of Atletico Madrid and Real Madrid who meet in the Spanish first division on Saturday (1930 GMT):

Playing style - Atletico play a fairly orthodox 4-4-2 formation, with Kiko Narvaez generally playing behind fellow striker Juan Eduardo Esnaider, and Juan Vizcaino linking the defence and the midfield. The back four pushes well forward to decrease opponents' room for manouevre, while goalkeeper Jose Molina plays as sweeper. Traditionally, Atletico have been a counter-attacking unit while Real Madrid have been a ball-playing outfit which tries to control the game. Radomir Antic's Atletico are no exception to this rule and are at their best bursting out of defence.

Strengths - Charismatic coach Antic turned relegation candidates into a double-winning side and as an unrivalled motivator continues to be the single most important factor behind Atletico's success. While Real often appear to be a group of highly-talented individuals, Antic has made Atletico a very cohesive unit. They haven't lost in 10 games and have recovered from a poor start to the season. The defence was the meanest in Spain last season. In midfield Caminero's vision and Kiko's cheeky improvisation are both potential match-winners, while Pantic's demon right foot has made set-pieces a major source of goals.

Weaknesses - Too many of Atletico's players are temperamental. Lopez, Caminero and Esnaider in particular are known to lose their heads and get sent off, and, along with Pantic, have too many off days. Atletico must wait to see if Argentine midfielder Diego Simeone has his suspension lifted ahead of the game. Without him they may lack the energy to win the midfield battle against Seedorf and Redondo. Caminero is likely to start but may still be suffering from a knock picked up last Sunday. They lack the strength in depth of Real, who usually leave a couple of internationals on the bench and several more in the stands. As a consequence Atletico have no experienced set-piece man to cover f

Motivation - Defeat would leave Atletico 11 points behind Real just before the half-way stage in the championship and would set up Real to take over as champions. Atletico lost both derbies last season and have not beaten their neighbours in the league since the 1991-92 season. The Atletico camp is tired of being ignored by the media while Real and Barcelona are given exhaustive coverage.
Probable team - Jose Molina, Toni Munoz, Roberto Solozabal, Delfi Geli, Santi Denia, Radek Bejbl, Milinko Pantic, Jose Luis Caminero, Juan Vizcaino, Kiko Narvaez, Juan Eduardo Esnaider.

Playing style - Fabio Capello also uses a fairly conventional 4-4-2 formation but has been widely criticised for negative tactics, excessive reliance on counter-attacks and for introducing a long ball philosophy to a group of skillful players capable of producing much better. Capello has strengthened his squad by buying a former protegee, Christian Panucci, during the month that the Spanish transfer market reopened. The ex-AC Milan man is expected to make his debut, taking Carlos Secretario's place on the right side of defence. Alongside him will be central defenders Fernando Hierro and Rafael Alkorta, with Roberto Carlos covering the left. Victor Sanchez, Fernando Redondo, Clarence Seed

Strengths - Goalkeeper Illgner is a tower of strength at the back, while both his substitutes, Canizares and Paco Buyo, would stroll into practically any European club side. Brazilian defender Roberto Carlos moves up well to create danger down the left while Fernando Hierro is not only the mainstay of the defence but is also strong coming forward through the middle. Both Roberto Carlos, whose swirling left-foot strikes have left several goalkeepers stranded already this season, and the right-footed Hierro are superb set-piece specialists. The same goes for the Balkan strike pair of Davor Suker and Predrag Mijatovic, and it is in their individual brilliance, together with that of teenager

Weaknesses - Under Capello Real have played effectively but with little style and still do not play well as a team. The side relies excessively on Mijatovic, Suker and Raul making the best out of half-chances. The long-ball philosophy, which Capello denies he employs, means at times the midfield seems not to exist at all. And there are problems at the back. Despite signing Illgner because of Capello's insistence on buying a taller keeper, Real have been particularly vulnerable in the air. Panucci is an international defender but playing a Madrid derby five days after arriving in Spain is really being thrown in at the deep end. Motivation - Victory would take Real a hefty six points clear of Barcelona at the top of the Spanish league, at least until Sunday. They also need to prove themselves as potential champions after their disappointing 0-0 draw at bottom-placed Extremadura last weekend.
Probable team - Bodo Illgner, Christian Panucci, Fernando Hierro, Rafael Alkorta, Roberto Carlos, Clarence Seedorf, Fernando Redondo, Victor Sanchez, Raul Gonzalez, Davor Suker, Predrag Mijatovic.
